```{python}
import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
prof = pd.read_csv("outputs/cluster_profiles.csv").set_index("cluster")
oy = pd.read_csv("outputs/outcomes_by_year.csv")
S = json.load(open("outputs/summary.json"))
names = prof["name"]
```

## The question

How do municipalities group by drinking-water safety and context, and how do infant
mortality, school results and dropout look in each group?

- `{python} f"{S['municipalities']:,}"` municipalities, 2016-2023
- IRCA = utility-supplied ("prestadores") water-risk index, INS open data

## The four clusters

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Named clusters: rows, municipalities, share of urban rows and median IRCA (utility-supplied)."
t = prof[["name", "rows", "municipalities", "urban_row_share", "irca_median"]].copy()
t["urban_row_share"] = (t["urban_row_share"] * 100).round(0).astype(int).astype(str) + "%"
t.columns = ["Cluster", "Rows", "Municipalities", "Urban rows", "Median IRCA"]
t.reset_index(drop=True).to_markdown(index=False)
```

## What sets them apart

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Cluster mean z-scores (within year) of nine profile features; blue below average, red above."
#| fig-alt: "Heatmap of nine profile features by four named clusters, blue below the yearly average and red above."
zc = [c for c in prof.columns if c.startswith("z_")]
M = prof[zc].T; M.index = [c[2:] for c in zc]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.2))
v = np.abs(M.values).max()
im = ax.imshow(M.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-v, vmax=v, aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(M.shape[1])); ax.set_xticklabels([names[c].replace(", ", ",\n") for c in M.columns], fontsize=7)
ax.set_yticks(range(M.shape[0])); ax.set_yticklabels(M.index, fontsize=8)
for i in range(M.shape[0]):
    for j in range(M.shape[1]):
        ax.text(j, i, f"{M.values[i, j]:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7)
fig.colorbar(im, label="mean z-score"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Outcomes by cluster

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Median infant mortality, Saber 11 score and dropout by cluster and year; gaps where a source has no data."
#| fig-alt: "Three line charts of outcomes by year for four clusters, with gaps in missing years."
years = np.arange(2016, 2024)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 3.4))
for ax, o in zip(axes, ["infant_mortality", "saber11_mean", "dropout_rate"]):
    for c, g in oy[oy["outcome"] == o].groupby("cluster"):
        ax.plot(years, g.set_index("year")["median"].reindex(years).values, marker="o", ms=3,
                color=prof.loc[c, "color"], label=names[c])
    ax.set_title(o, fontsize=9); ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
fig.legend(*axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, fontsize=6)
plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.14, 1, 1)); plt.show()
```

## What this does and does not show

- Shows: municipalities fall into four water-and-context profiles; outcomes differ by profile
- Does not show: that water quality causes any outcome
- Confounders: poverty, health services, altitude, rurality
- Gaps: infant mortality method changes in 2017; Saber 11 has no 2018 or 2021
